source.title: Exploring dark knowledge under various teacher capacities and addressing capacity mismatch
source.authors: Xin-Chun Li; Wen-Shu Fan; Bowen Tao; Le Gan; De-Chuan Zhan

record.tranche_reason: The study examines teacher output probabilities and class affinities in knowledge distillation, not convergence of internal representations or distances between inputs. Its results therefore do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own measurements of output-level class-affinity consistency and wrong-class probability variation. These are related to, but distinct from, representation alignment as defined in the claim; they are recorded under fits_no_version. It also cites work on convergent learning, but does not test that work's representation claim.
record.test_reason: The study measures agreement in output class rankings, and wrong-class probability spread, between knowledge-distillation teachers of different capacity. It does not measure alignment of internal representations, such as kernel or neighbour similarity, across models, and it does not test whether alignment grows with scale. The feature-angle analysis in Fig. 3 describes within-model class geometry, not cross-model alignment. Convergent learning (ref 73) is cited only in passing, to note that output orders differ even across seeds. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses'.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors find two things: larger teachers give less distinct non-ground-truth probabilities, and teachers agree on relative class affinity. They argue the first causes capacity mismatch in knowledge distillation. The paraphrase should add that they propose FGCR, RegT and ISATS to fix this, with ISATS performing best.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures output probabilities and class rankings for knowledge distillation; it does not apply a representation-convergence method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported measurements vary by dataset, teacher capacity or architecture, and, for the affinity analysis, the chosen ranking metric and class-affinity rules.

fits_no_version.finding: Teachers of different capacity and architecture largely agree on output-level relative class rankings (Spearman >0.85 on CIFAR-10; Kendall's tau implies about 0.875 pairwise agreement). Wrong-class probability spread shrinks as teachers get larger.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Classifiers of different capacity trained on the same data share output-level relative class-affinity rankings, while larger ones give flatter non-ground-truth probabilities.

record.problems: The study measures output probabilities and class rankings rather than representation-space distances. Some class-affinity rankings are manually defined from averaged posterior distributions, and several comparisons are presented graphically.
record.rows_left_out: The per-rule entries in Table 1 are not listed separately; the reported average over rules is recorded instead. Additional individual top-K overlap distributions in Fig. 5, metric curves in Fig. 6, and visual examples in Figs. 1 and 7 are omitted because they concern the same output-level class-affinity construct and are not representation measures.

untested.parts: All: no cross-model representation alignment measured as a function of scale.
All: no cross-seed feature or subspace comparison; seed variation is only cited.
All: no mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer.
All: no interpretable features or circuits compared across models.
All: no representation-similarity metric sensitivity analysis.
All: no analysis of incompleteness or causes of representation alignment.

record.verdict_notes: All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The output-rank consistency across capacities is superficially related to V1, but it is a different construct: per-sample class-rank agreement of logits, not representational alignment, and with no trend of growing agreement with scale. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Representation alignment across models as size and capability increase, including similarity of distances between the same inputs.
Cross-modal alignment between vision and language models on paired inputs.
Shared features or subspaces across independently initialized models of the same architecture.
Mapping, stitching, or otherwise transferring representations between models.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
Dependence of representation-convergence measurements on similarity metric, settings, or input distribution.
Whether representation alignment is incomplete or explained by shared data or objectives.
